items.stem: Define the term 'economic growth'.
items.answer: An increase in the real value of a country's output (real GDP) over time.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, an increase in the real value of a country's output (real GDP) over time. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between nominal GDP growth and real GDP growth.
items.answer: Nominal growth measures the rise in the money value of output; real growth removes the effect of inflation, so it measures the change in the volume of output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark nominal = money value at current prices; 1 mark real = adjusted for inflation / volume of output. [2]

items.stem: Explain why low and stable inflation benefits businesses as well as consumers.
items.answer: Stable prices make costs and revenues predictable, so firms can plan and invest with confidence; consumers keep their purchasing power so demand is steadier; exports stay price-competitive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark planning/certainty; 1 mark investment confidence or stable demand; 1 mark international competitiveness. [3]

items.stem: Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd, a private limited company in South Africa with about 140 employees, brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets. Explain how an increase in the inflation rate in South Africa from 3% to 9% could affect Cape Brew.
items.answer: Points to develop for Cape Brew: inflation means a sustained rise in the general price level; higher input and wage costs squeeze profit margins unless prices rise; falling real incomes reduce demand, especially for income-elastic craft beer and soft drinks; if inflation is higher than in trading partners, exports lose price competitiveness.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: inflation means a sustained rise in the general price level. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Cape Brew: beverages, about 140 employees, private limited company in South Africa; demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Cape Brew, e.g. higher input and wage costs squeeze profit margins unless prices rise; falling real incomes reduce demand, especially for income-elastic craft beer and soft drinks; if inflation is higher than in trading partners, exports lose price competitiveness. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Nusantara Apparel Tbk is a public limited company based in Jakarta, Indonesia. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands and employs about 4,000 people. A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Explain how faster economic growth in Indonesia could affect both the revenue and the costs of Nusantara Apparel.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: real GDP growth raises incomes and demand; revenue rises, more so if sportswear are income elastic; skills shortages and rising wages increase costs; need to expand capacity may require investment and finance.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: real GDP growth raises incomes and demand. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, about 4,000 employees, public limited company in Indonesia; a global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Nusantara Apparel, e.g. revenue rises, more so if sportswear are income elastic; skills shortages and rising wages increase costs; need to expand capacity may require investment and finance. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

The business has around 140 employees. Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Explain how faster economic growth in South Africa could affect both the revenue and the costs of Cape Brew.
items.answer: Points to develop for Cape Brew: real GDP growth raises incomes and demand; revenue rises, more so if craft beer and soft drinks are income elastic; skills shortages and rising wages increase costs; need to expand capacity may require investment and finance.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: real GDP growth raises incomes and demand. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Cape Brew: beverages, about 140 employees, private limited company in South Africa; demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Cape Brew, e.g. revenue rises, more so if craft beer and soft drinks are income elastic; skills shortages and rising wages increase costs; need to expand capacity may require investment and finance. items.stem: Based in Lima, Andes Textil SA (family-owned private company) makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan. The business has around 320 employees. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Discuss whether Andes Textil should postpone its planned expansion because economic growth in Peru is forecast to slow to 0.5%.
items.answer: For: lower growth means weaker demand and spare capacity; expansion financed by borrowing increases risk; cash could be kept as a buffer. Against: forecasts are often wrong and the slowdown may be brief; costs of building and recruiting may be lower in a slowdown; expansion may target export markets that are still growing. Judgement: the decision for Andes Textil depends mainly on the income elasticity of demand for its alpaca knitwear, and also on how the expansion is financed.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Andes Textil: textile manufacturing, about 320 employees, family-owned private company in Peru; the founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. lower growth means weaker demand and spare capacity; expansion financed by borrowing increases risk; cash could be kept as a buffer; arguments against, e.g. forecasts are often wrong and the slowdown may be brief; costs of building and recruiting may be lower in a slowdown; expansion may target export markets that are still growing. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the income elasticity of demand for its alpaca knitwear; how the expansion is financed; the strategic importance of moving ahead of competitors. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Andes Textil, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Based in Karachi, Indus Sports Goods Ltd (private limited company) makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. The business has around 950 employees. A rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices. Using the case and your own knowledge, evaluate the extent to which high inflation is the most serious macroeconomic problem facing Indus Sports.
items.answer: For: rising costs of materials and labour cut margins; uncertainty discourages investment; loss of export competitiveness. Against: unemployment or a recession may reduce demand by more; exchange-rate movements may matter more for a business that trades internationally; if demand is price inelastic, cost increases can be passed on. Judgement: the decision for Indus Sports depends mainly on how price elastic demand for its footballs and cricket equipment is, and also on the share of its sales that are exported.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Indus Sports: sports equipment manufacturing, about 950 employees, private limited company in Pakistan; a rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. rising costs of materials and labour cut margins; uncertainty discourages investment; loss of export competitiveness; arguments against, e.g. unemployment or a recession may reduce demand by more; exchange-rate movements may matter more for a business that trades internationally; if demand is price inelastic, cost increases can be passed on. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how price elastic demand for its footballs and cricket equipment is; the share of its sales that are exported; whether its competitors face the same pressures. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Indus Sports, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Which type of unemployment is caused by the long-term decline of an industry?
items.answer: Structural unemployment
items.markingKey: Structural unemployment. Structural unemployment arises when the skills of workers no longer match the jobs available, e.g. after an industry declines.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'unemployment'?
options: Reducing the risk of exchange-rate changes, e.g. by agreeing today a fixed rate for a future currency transaction (a forward contract).
The cost of borrowing money and the reward for saving, expressed as a percentage of the sum borrowed or saved per year.
The situation where people of working age who are willing and able to work, and are actively seeking a job, cannot find one.
The total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year, adjusted to remove the effect of inflation.
items.answer: The situation where people of working age who are willing and able to work, and are actively seeking a job, cannot find one.
items.markingKey: unemployment: The situation where people of working age who are willing and able to work, and are actively seeking a job, cannot find one.

items.stem: Explain two ways in which rising unemployment can affect a business that sells luxury products.
items.answer: Demand falls because household incomes fall and luxuries are income elastic; but the business finds it easier and cheaper to recruit staff because more people are looking for work.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark effect, 1 mark explanation): falling demand (income elastic); easier recruitment / less wage pressure. [4]

items.stem: A country has a labour force of 8.8 million people, of whom 0.66 million are unemployed. What is the unemployment rate?
items.markingKey: Unemployment rate = unemployed / labour force × 100 = 0.66 / 8.8 × 100 = 7.5%.

Against: unemployment or a recession may reduce demand by more; exchange-rate movements may matter more for a business that trades internationally; if demand is price inelastic, cost increases can be passed on. Judgement: the decision for Nile Pharma depends mainly on how price elastic demand for its generic medicines is, and also on the share of its sales that are exported.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how price elastic demand for its generic medicines is; the share of its sales that are exported; whether its competitors face the same pressures. items.stem: Define the term 'business cycle'.
items.answer: The regular pattern of rises and falls in real GDP over time, through the phases of boom, downturn, recession and recovery.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the regular pattern of rises and falls in real GDP over time, through the phases of boom, downturn, recession and recovery. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business selling luxury products is likely to be affected more by the business cycle than one selling basic foods.
items.answer: Luxuries have high positive income elasticity, so demand rises and falls more than incomes; basic foods have low income elasticity, so demand is stable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark income elasticity idea; 1 mark luxuries elastic/large swings; 1 mark necessities stable. [3]

items.stem: Explain one way a business could use knowledge of the business cycle when planning capacity.
items.answer: It could avoid committing to large fixed-cost expansion near the peak of a boom and instead invest during recovery, so new capacity arrives as demand rises.
items.markingKey: 1 mark planning action; 1 mark link to cycle phase and demand. [2]

items.stem: Muscat Dates & Co. LLC is a family-owned limited company based in Muscat, Oman. It processes, packs and exports dates and date syrup and employs about 160 people. Three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor. Explain how a recession in Oman is likely to affect Muscat Dates.
items.answer: Points to develop for Muscat Dates: recession is falling real GDP and incomes; demand for packed dates and date syrup falls, especially if income elastic; lower capacity utilisation raises unit fixed costs; cash-flow problems and possible redundancies affect morale.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: recession is falling real GDP and incomes. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Muscat Dates: food processing, about 160 employees, family-owned limited company in Oman; three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Muscat Dates, e.g. demand for packed dates and date syrup falls, especially if income elastic; lower capacity utilisation raises unit fixed costs; cash-flow problems and possible redundancies affect morale. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd, a private limited company in South Africa with about 140 employees, brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets. Explain how Cape Brew might be affected as South Africa moves from recession into recovery.
items.answer: Points to develop for Cape Brew: incomes and confidence start to rise; sales of craft beer and soft drinks increase, so spare capacity is used; need for working capital rises as output grows; may need to recruit and train staff again.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: incomes and confidence start to rise. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Cape Brew: beverages, about 140 employees, private limited company in South Africa; demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Cape Brew, e.g. sales of craft beer and soft drinks increase, so spare capacity is used; need for working capital rises as output grows; may need to recruit and train staff again. items.stem: Based in Lagos, Lagos Bites Ltd (private limited company) produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. The business has around 700 employees. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Evaluate the most suitable strategy for Lagos Bites if Nigeria enters a recession next year.
items.answer: For: cost cutting protects profit and cash; a value range of packaged snacks keeps price-sensitive customers; export growth spreads risk. Against: cost cutting can damage quality and morale; lower prices may harm the brand; export markets may also be in recession. Judgement: the decision for Lagos Bites depends mainly on the income elasticity of demand for its packaged snacks, and also on its cash reserves and gearing.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Lagos Bites: food processing, about 700 employees, private limited company in Nigeria; rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. cost cutting protects profit and cash; a value range of packaged snacks keeps price-sensitive customers; export growth spreads risk; arguments against, e.g. cost cutting can damage quality and morale; lower prices may harm the brand; export markets may also be in recession. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the income elasticity of demand for its packaged snacks; its cash reserves and gearing; how long the recession lasts. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Lagos Bites, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Based in Hanoi, Mekong Furniture JSC (joint stock company) makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe. The business has around 1,200 employees. A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. Explain one disadvantage to Mekong Furniture of investing in new capacity during an economic recovery.
items.answer: The recovery may stall, leaving spare capacity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. the recovery may stall, leaving spare capacity; borrowing increases gearing and interest costs; cash flow pressure before sales rise. 1 mark: explained in the context of Mekong Furniture (furniture manufacturing). [2]

items.stem: IslaConnect Inc. sells 80,000 units a month of a product with an income elasticity of demand of 0.4. Real incomes in the Philippines are forecast to change by -4% as the business cycle turns down. Calculate the expected monthly sales after the change.
items.answer: 78,720 units a month (-1.6%)

items.stem: Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Lumen Robotics plc, a public limited company in Singapore with about 2,400 employees, designs and builds robots used on factory assembly lines. Explain how a recession in Singapore is likely to affect Lumen Robotics, and judge which point is most important for Lumen Robotics.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lumen Robotics: recession is falling real GDP and incomes; demand for industrial robots falls, especially if income elastic; lower capacity utilisation raises unit fixed costs; cash-flow problems and possible redundancies affect morale.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: recession is falling real GDP and incomes. items.stem: Define the term 'fiscal policy'.
items.answer: Government decisions on taxation and government spending used to influence the level of economic activity.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, government decisions on taxation and government spending used to influence the level of economic activity. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a rise in interest rates is likely to reduce demand for consumer durables such as cars.
items.answer: Many durables are bought on credit, so higher rates raise monthly repayments; higher mortgage costs also reduce disposable income, and saving becomes more attractive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark credit cost; 1 mark lower disposable income / incentive to save. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a cut in corporation tax might encourage businesses to invest.
items.answer: Firms keep a larger share of profit, so more retained earnings are available and the after-tax return on new projects rises.
items.markingKey: 1 mark more retained profit; 1 mark higher after-tax return. [2]

items.stem: Tejo Mobility SA is a public limited company based in Lisbon, Portugal. It assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union and employs about 600 people. Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Explain how government supply-side policies to improve training could affect Tejo Mobility.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tejo Mobility: supply-side policy raises productive potential; better-skilled workers raise labour productivity; lower recruitment and training costs; improved competitiveness against foreign rivals.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: supply-side policy raises productive potential. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Tejo Mobility: vehicle manufacturing, about 600 employees, public limited company in Portugal; battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Tejo Mobility, e.g. better-skilled workers raise labour productivity; lower recruitment and training costs; improved competitiveness against foreign rivals. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Inflation in Turkey has been above 40% for two years. Bosphorus Home AŞ, a public limited company in Turkey with about 3,500 employees, makes washing machines, fridges and ovens sold in Europe and the Middle East. Discuss the extent to which government economic policies in Turkey are likely to affect the success of Bosphorus Home.
items.answer: For: interest rates affect borrowing costs and demand; tax changes affect prices and profits; supply-side policies affect skills and costs. Against: internal factors such as management and products matter more; competition and global demand may dominate; policies may change before they have effect. Judgement: the decision for Bosphorus Home depends mainly on how much it borrows and exports, and also on the size and timing of policy changes.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how much it borrows and exports; the size and timing of policy changes; the quality of its strategy. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Bosphorus Home, not a generic one. [12]

items.answer: May be financed by higher taxes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. may be financed by higher taxes; could push up wages and interest rates; benefits take years to arrive. 1 mark: explained in the context of Lagos Bites (food processing). [2]

items.stem: Lagos Bites Ltd has variable-rate loans of $10 million and an operating profit of $2,500,000. The central bank raises interest rates so that its loan rate rises from 6% to 7.5%. Calculate the increase in annual interest payments.
items.answer: Interest rises by $150,000
items.markingKey: Interest before = $600,000, after = $750,000 [1]; increase = $150,000 [1]. [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'exchange rate'.
items.answer: The price of one currency expressed in terms of another currency.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the price of one currency expressed in terms of another currency. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a depreciation of a country's currency is not always good for its exporters.
items.answer: Exports become cheaper abroad, but imported components and fuel cost more, raising costs; if foreign demand is price inelastic, volume gains are small.
items.markingKey: 1 mark cheaper exports; 1 mark higher import costs; 1 mark elasticity. [3]

items.stem: Explain how a business could reduce the risk caused by exchange-rate changes.
items.answer: It could hedge using forward contracts, invoice in its own currency, or match costs and revenues in the same currency (e.g. by producing abroad).
items.markingKey: 1 mark method; 1 mark explanation of how it reduces risk. [2]

items.stem: Based in Bogotá, Café Cordillera SAS (private limited company) roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. The business has around 900 employees. The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Explain the likely effects on Café Cordillera of a large and sudden depreciation of the Colombian peso.
items.answer: Points to develop for Café Cordillera: depreciation lowers foreign prices of exports; imported materials become more expensive; margins depend on how much of the cost base is imported; uncertainty makes pricing and planning harder.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: depreciation lowers foreign prices of exports. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Café Cordillera: food and drink retail, about 900 employees, private limited company in Colombia; the owners want to double the number of cafés within three years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Café Cordillera, e.g. imported materials become more expensive; margins depend on how much of the cost base is imported; uncertainty makes pricing and planning harder. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Explain how an appreciation of its currency could benefit a business.
items.answer: Imported materials, components and machinery become cheaper in home currency, cutting costs and raising margins on domestic sales.
items.markingKey: 1 mark cheaper imports; 1 mark effect on costs/margins. [2]

items.stem: Which business term is described here: "An increase in the real value of a country's output (real GDP) over time."
items.answer: economic growth
items.markingKey: This is the definition of economic growth.

items.answer: Costs of materials and wages rise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. costs of materials and wages rise; customers' real incomes fall so demand may fall; it becomes harder to plan and its exports become less price competitive. 1 mark: explained in the context of Muscat Dates (food processing). [2]

items.stem: Explain why a government may find it difficult to achieve all of its macroeconomic objectives at the same time.
items.answer: Objectives conflict: policies that boost growth and reduce unemployment can raise inflation and worsen the trade balance; reducing inflation with higher interest rates can slow growth and raise unemployment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark idea of conflicting objectives; 2 marks a developed example (e.g. growth v inflation trade-off). [3]

items.stem: In a country with a labour force of 24 million, the number unemployed changed from 1.92 million to 2.64 million over a year (labour force unchanged). Calculate the unemployment rate in each year.

Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Kiwi Trails Ltd, a private limited company in New Zealand with about 90 employees, runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours. Explain how an increase in the inflation rate in New Zealand from 3% to 9% could affect Kiwi Trails.
items.answer: Points to develop for Kiwi Trails: inflation means a sustained rise in the general price level; higher input and wage costs squeeze profit margins unless prices rise; falling real incomes reduce demand, especially for income-elastic adventure tours; if inflation is higher than in trading partners, exports lose price competitiveness.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: inflation means a sustained rise in the general price level. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Kiwi Trails: tourism, about 90 employees, private limited company in New Zealand; bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Kiwi Trails, e.g. higher input and wage costs squeeze profit margins unless prices rise; falling real incomes reduce demand, especially for income-elastic adventure tours; if inflation is higher than in trading partners, exports lose price competitiveness. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Seoul, Han River Games Co. (private limited company) develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases. The business has around 340 employees. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. (a) Define 'unemployment'. (b) Explain one advantage to Han River Games of a period of rapid economic growth in South Korea.
items.answer: (a) The situation where people of working age who are willing and able to work, and are actively seeking a job, cannot find one. (b) Rising household incomes increase demand for its mobile games.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (rising household incomes increase demand for its mobile games; higher sales allow economies of scale; easier to raise finance as banks and investors are confident), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Han River Games [3]

items.stem: In which phase of the business cycle are capacity shortages and rising inflation most likely?
items.answer: Boom
items.markingKey: Boom. In a boom demand exceeds capacity, so firms face shortages of labour and materials and prices rise.

items.stem: Explain why a business may cut prices during a recession even though this reduces its profit margin.
items.answer: To protect sales volume and market share when consumers trade down; keeping capacity utilised spreads fixed costs and keeps cash flowing.
items.markingKey: 1 mark protect volume/market share; 1 mark fixed costs/cash flow. [2]

items.stem: Based in Lima, Andes Textil SA (family-owned private company) makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan. The business has around 320 employees. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Explain two strategies Andes Textil could use to reduce the impact of a recession.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andes Textil: cost reduction (e.g. renegotiating supplier contracts, delayering); introducing lower-priced versions of alpaca knitwear; diversifying into less cyclical markets or export markets; protecting cash flow by reducing inventory and credit periods.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: cost reduction (e.g. renegotiating supplier contracts, delayering). AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Andes Textil: textile manufacturing, about 320 employees, family-owned private company in Peru; the founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Andes Textil, e.g. introducing lower-priced versions of alpaca knitwear; diversifying into less cyclical markets or export markets; protecting cash flow by reducing inventory and credit periods. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Nile Pharma plc sells 80,000 units a month of a product with an income elasticity of demand of 2.5. Real incomes in Egypt are forecast to change by -3% as the business cycle turns down. Calculate the expected monthly sales after the change and the change in monthly revenue if the price is $20.
items.answer: 74,000 units a month (-7.5%)

items.stem: Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Tejo Mobility SA, a public limited company in Portugal with about 600 employees, assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union. Using the case and your own knowledge, evaluate the most suitable strategy for Tejo Mobility if Portugal enters a recession next year.
items.answer: For: cost cutting protects profit and cash; a value range of electric scooters and e-bikes keeps price-sensitive customers; export growth spreads risk. Against: cost cutting can damage quality and morale; lower prices may harm the brand; export markets may also be in recession. Judgement: the decision for Tejo Mobility depends mainly on the income elasticity of demand for its electric scooters and e-bikes, and also on its cash reserves and gearing.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Tejo Mobility: vehicle manufacturing, about 600 employees, public limited company in Portugal; battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. cost cutting protects profit and cash; a value range of electric scooters and e-bikes keeps price-sensitive customers; export growth spreads risk; arguments against, e.g. cost cutting can damage quality and morale; lower prices may harm the brand; export markets may also be in recession. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the income elasticity of demand for its electric scooters and e-bikes; its cash reserves and gearing; how long the recession lasts. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Tejo Mobility, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Which business term is described here: "Decisions by the central bank on interest rates and the money supply, used mainly to control inflation."
items.answer: monetary policy
items.markingKey: This is the definition of monetary policy.

items.stem: Explain the difference between fiscal policy and monetary policy.
items.answer: Fiscal policy is government taxation and spending; monetary policy is the central bank's control of interest rates and the money supply.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each correct description. [2]

items.stem: Lanka Tea Estates plc has variable-rate loans of $4 million and an operating profit of $600,000. The central bank raises interest rates so that its loan rate rises from 3% to 5%. Calculate the increase in annual interest payments.
items.answer: Interest rises by $80,000
items.markingKey: Interest before = $120,000, after = $200,000 [1]; increase = $80,000 [1]. [2]

items.stem: Mekong Furniture JSC has variable-rate loans of $10 million and an operating profit of $3,000,000. The central bank raises interest rates so that its loan rate rises from 3% to 5%. Calculate the increase in annual interest payments and the percentage fall in profit before tax.
items.answer: Interest rises by $200,000; PBT falls by 7.4%
items.markingKey: Interest before = $300,000, after = $500,000 [1]; increase = $200,000 [1]; PBT falls from $2,700,000 to $2,500,000, a fall of 7.4% [1]. [3]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Evaluate whether a cut in corporation tax or a cut in interest rates would benefit Pearl Logistics more.
items.answer: For: a tax cut raises retained profit for investment; an interest cut reduces borrowing costs; an interest cut may boost consumer demand. Against: a tax cut helps only if the business is profitable; an interest cut helps little if it has no debt; effects take time and depend on confidence. Judgement: the decision for Pearl Logistics depends mainly on its current profitability and gearing, and also on whether its customers buy freight and warehousing services on credit.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Pearl Logistics: logistics, about 1,500 employees, private limited company in Qatar; large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery). AO3 Analysis [6]: arguments for, e.g. a tax cut raises retained profit for investment; an interest cut reduces borrowing costs; an interest cut may boost consumer demand; arguments against, e.g. a tax cut helps only if the business is profitable; an interest cut helps little if it has no debt; effects take time and depend on confidence. AO4 Evaluation [8]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its current profitability and gearing; whether its customers buy freight and warehousing services on credit; the size of each change. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Pearl Logistics, not a generic one. [20]

items.stem: Based in Madrid, Iberia Moda SA (public limited company) runs 180 fast-fashion clothing stores and an online shop. The business has around 6,000 employees. Online sales are growing quickly while sales in its high-street stores are falling. Explain one advantage to Iberia Moda of a 15% depreciation of the euro.
items.answer: Its exports become cheaper in foreign currencies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. its exports become cheaper in foreign currencies; imported rival products become dearer in Spain; foreign-currency revenue is worth more in euros. 1 mark: explained in the context of Iberia Moda (clothing retail). [2]

items.stem: Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd is a private limited company based in Bangkok, Thailand. It produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores and employs about 1,100 people. Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Siam Ready Meals of a 15% depreciation of the Thai baht.
items.answer: Advantage: its exports become cheaper in foreign currencies. Disadvantage: imported materials and components cost more.
items.markingKey: For each point: 1 mark identification, 1 mark explanation applied to Siam Ready Meals. Advantages: its exports become cheaper in foreign currencies; imported rival products become dearer in Thailand; foreign-currency revenue is worth more in Thai baht. Disadvantages: imported materials and components cost more; foreign-currency loans become more expensive to repay; higher import prices may raise inflation and wage claims. [4]

(b) Explain one advantage to Lumen Robotics of invoicing its overseas customers in Singapore dollars rather than US dollars.
items.answer: (a) Reducing the risk of exchange-rate changes, e.g. by agreeing today a fixed rate for a future currency transaction (a forward contract). (b) It knows exactly how much revenue it will receive.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (it knows exactly how much revenue it will receive; no need to pay for hedging; simpler cash-flow forecasting), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Lumen Robotics [3]

items.stem: Which group is most likely to gain from an unexpected rise in inflation?
options: Banks lending at fixed interest rates
items.answer: Businesses with large fixed-interest loans
items.markingKey: Businesses with large fixed-interest loans. Inflation reduces the real value of debt, so fixed-rate borrowers gain while lenders and savers lose.

items.stem: Andina Solar SpA is a private limited company based in Santiago, Chile. It designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes and employs about 380 people. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Explain one advantage to Andina Solar of inflation of about 8% a year in Chile.
items.answer: It may be able to raise its prices without losing customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. it may be able to raise its prices without losing customers; the real value of its debts falls; the value of its stocks of materials rises. 1 mark: explained in the context of Andina Solar (renewable energy). [2]

A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. items.answer: Opportunity: it may be able to raise its prices without losing customers. Threat: costs of materials and wages rise.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark application to Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, 4,000 employees). Explain how faster economic growth in Sri Lanka could affect both the revenue and the costs of Lanka Tea.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: real GDP growth raises incomes and demand; revenue rises, more so if packaged tea are income elastic; skills shortages and rising wages increase costs; need to expand capacity may require investment and finance.

items.answer: (a) The situation where people of working age who are willing and able to work, and are actively seeking a job, cannot find one. (b) Rising household incomes increase demand for its mobile payment services.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (rising household incomes increase demand for its mobile payment services; higher sales allow economies of scale; easier to raise finance as banks and investors are confident), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to BatikPay [3]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'recession'?
options: The total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year, adjusted to remove the effect of inflation.
The regular pattern of rises and falls in real GDP over time, through the phases of boom, downturn, recession and recovery.
A period of falling real GDP, often defined as two consecutive quarters of negative economic growth.
Reducing the risk of exchange-rate changes, e.g. by agreeing today a fixed rate for a future currency transaction (a forward contract).
items.answer: A period of falling real GDP, often defined as two consecutive quarters of negative economic growth.
items.markingKey: recession: A period of falling real GDP, often defined as two consecutive quarters of negative economic growth.

items.stem: IslaConnect Inc. is a private limited company based in Manila, the Philippines. It runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia and employs about 2,600 people. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Explain one advantage to IslaConnect of investing in new capacity during an economic recovery.
items.answer: Ready to meet rising demand before rivals.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. ready to meet rising demand before rivals; building and equipment costs may still be low; gains economies of scale as output rises. 1 mark: explained in the context of IslaConnect (business process outsourcing). [2]

items.stem: Lanka Tea Estates plc is a public limited company based in Colombo, Sri Lanka. It grows, processes and packs tea on its own estates and employs about 5,000 people. Many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities. Explain how a recession in Sri Lanka is likely to affect Lanka Tea.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: recession is falling real GDP and incomes; demand for packaged tea falls, especially if income elastic; lower capacity utilisation raises unit fixed costs; cash-flow problems and possible redundancies affect morale.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: recession is falling real GDP and incomes. items.answer: 60,600 units a month (+1.0%)

(a) Analyse two strategies Lumen Robotics could use to reduce the impact of a recession. (b) Discuss whether Lumen Robotics should increase its capacity now that Singapore's economy is in the recovery phase of the business cycle.
items.answer: (a) Cost reduction (e.g. renegotiating supplier contracts, delayering); introducing lower-priced versions of industrial robots; diversifying into less cyclical markets or export markets; protecting cash flow by reducing inventory and credit periods. (b) For: demand for industrial robots is likely to rise; acting early may gain market share; construction and equipment costs may be lower now. Against: recovery may be weak or short; borrowing increases risk; existing spare capacity could be used first. Judgement: the decision for Lumen Robotics depends mainly on the accuracy of economic forecasts, and also on current capacity utilisation.
